 2. The criminal law has been set into motion based on the first information statement of Sujata Shivaraj.
The gist of the prosecution case is that the accused No.1 married CW-1 on 06-05- 2011.
At the time of marriage, the accused have demanded and taken gold ornaments and silver articles as dowry from the complainant and her parents.
After the marriage, the accused have subjected CW-1 to mental and physical cruelty in respect of dowry by demanding complainant to bring additional dowry from her father and elder sister.

It is further alleged that when the accused visited the house of complainant to see new born baby girl the accused stated that "she is not my daughter and she is born to someone" and started quarreling with the complainant and assaulted CW-1 with hands causing bodily pain, abused the complainant in filthy language and threatened the complainant with dire consequences.
Based on the said information, a case in  3  C.C.No.2937/2024 Cr.No.322/2022 came to be registered against the accused for the aforesaid offences.
3. After completion of the investigation, the P..I of Basavanagudi Women P.S. has filed chargesheet against accused for the aforesaid offences.
On receipt of charge sheet, this court took cognizance of the alleged offences.
Pursuant to the issuance and service of summons, accused entered appearance and was enlarged on bail.

The prosecution papers was furnished to the accused as required U/s.207 of Cr.P.C.

sentences.text: 9 . POINT No.1 :- It is the fundamental principle of criminal jurisprudence that the prosecution has to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt.

In order to bring home the guilt of the accused,
the prosecution has examined one witness as PW-1 got marked Ex.P.1 to Ex.P3 documents.
Ex.P1 is the first information  5  C.C.No.2937/2024 statement.
Ex.P.2 is the spot panchanama.
Ex.P.3 is further statement of complainant.
was examined as PW-1 Smt.Sujatha.

She in her examination-in-chief has deposed that her marriage with accused No.1 was performed on 06-05-2011 and deposed after the marriage, accused looked after her well and deposed accused did not subjected her to any physical and mental cruelty, in demand of dowry and never assaulted her, abused her and threatened to kill her.
PW-1 deposed that there was petty quarrel between her and accused in respect to family issues, for which she went to the police station.
There the police have took her signatures on documents.
PW-1 identified Ex.P.1 first information statement and also identified her signature at Ex.P1.
PW-1 also identified Ex.P.2 spot Panchanama and her signature at Ex.P2 and she pleaded her ignorance about the contents of Ex.P.1 and P.2.
The learned Sr.APP treated PW-1 as hostile witness and cross examined her.
During which PW-1 admitted that she and accused have compromised the matter and denied all other suggestions.

11. On appreciation of entire materials on record, it is Sujatha Shivaraj vs Madivalappa G on 5 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97111386/
4 apparent that PW-1 being the informant, key and material witness  6  C.C.No.2937/2024 have turned hostile to the prosecution case.
Therefore, this court was pleased to reject the prayer of the learned Sr.APP to summon other chargesheeted witnesses.

Even, if the summons was issued to other chargesheeted witnesses, no purpose would be served as the material witness has given go-bye to her own statement and also the valuable time of the court would be saved.
As such other charge sheeted witnesses were dropped and prosecution evidence was taken as closed.
In view of the material witness, turning hostile the prosecution has failed to bring home the guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubt.
Accordingly, I answer Point No.1 in the Negative.

12. POINT No.2:- For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
 ORDER
In exercise of power conferred Under Section 248(1) of Cr.P.C., Accused No.1 is acquitted of the offences punishable U/s. 498A,323, 504, 506 of IPC. & Sec.3 & 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
The bail bonds of accused No.1 shall be in force for a period of 6 months.
